classification_statement: L1a linear-vacuum equivalent-current screening of axisymmetric PPM-stack geometries (geometry schema v1.1, the sweep-v2 builder rules on a wider box) with the cusp topology search v3.1 wall-cusp definition imported unchanged and the HEMP design ratio rho of Koch et al. reported per cusp. Nothing here is a plasma, mirror-probability, wall-loss, thrust or performance claim; rho and every mirror descriptor are field ratios of a screening field. The L1a field omits the soft-iron pole pieces and yoke that the geometry declares; for r_w / L > 0.5 the TWT/PPM review recommends an L1b (material-aware) or P2 confirmation before any absolute-field or rho-based design claim - that confirmation is queued, not run here.
purpose: Extend the L1a design space into the HEMP-like regime in which the wall cusp is a genuine field maximum of its cell relative to the adjacent axis peak (Koch design ratio rho >= 1.5), by varying the wall-radius-to-pitch ratio x_w = pi r_w / L (short pitch relative to bore) and the magnet radial thickness / inner radius, with 3-5 full-strength alternating stages. The TWT/PPM review (modern/docs/literature/twt-ppm-physics-for-hemp.md, commit beb4772c, sections 2.2, 4.4, 5.3 and the summary table row 5) established that every recorded field is a single-harmonic PPM field whose wall-cusp |B| is only I_1(x_w) = 0.45-0.61 of the axis peak, so in the sweep-v2 catalogue (x_w = 0.72-1.55) the cusp is the |B| minimum of its cell and rho = 1.5-10.6 (Koch et al. IEPC-2011-236 / IEPC-2007-110) is unreachable: the original study's parameterisation never varied r_w / L into the HEMP regime.
relation_to_prior_work: sweep v2 (modern/experiments/l1a_geometry_sweep_v2, preregistration 092f5fae, 96 accepted designs, r_w / L = 0.215-0.579) is reproduced here as a held-out set through the identity-proven pipeline of the wall-loss geometry screening v1 and is a strict subset of the v3 box; cusp topology search v3.1 (result cec47f12, 281/281 stable) supplies the wall-cusp definition and its code is imported, never re-implemented; no prior results/ directory, frozen preregistration file, cft_revival.plasma module or FYP/ file is modified.

koch_rho.citation: Koch, N., Harmann, H.-P., Kornfeld, G., Status of the THALES High Efficiency Multi Stage Plasma Thruster Development for HEMP-T 3050 and HEMP-T 30250, IEPC-2007-110 (2007), Table 1 (rho = 1.53 / 1.70 / 3.07 for DM9-1 and 4.07 / 4.2 / 10.57 for DM10); Koch et al., The HEMPT Concept - A Survey on Theoretical Considerations and Experimental Evidences, IEPC-2011-236 (2011)
koch_rho.quotation: High reflection of electrons in the cusp-mirror situation is achieved for a high ratio of the (predominantly radial) magnetic field strength at the inner discharge tube radius at the cusp middle plane to the (predominantly axial) magnetic field strength downstream the cusp.
koch_rho.radius_of_downstream_field: not stated in the paper (review section 8); the axis reading is used here, the wall reading is reported alongside
koch_rho.rho_downstream: |B|(r_w, z_c) / max |B_z(0, z)| over the axis interval from the cusp's axis null to the next axis null downstream (larger z) - Koch's wording, axis reading
koch_rho.rho_upstream: the same ratio with the upstream axis interval
koch_rho.rho_conservative: |B|(r_w, z_c) / max(upstream axis peak, downstream axis peak) - the binding HEMP-like classifier
koch_rho.rho_permissive: |B|(r_w, z_c) / min(upstream axis peak, downstream axis peak) - reported
koch_rho.rho_wall: |B|(r_w, z_c) / max |B|(r_w, z) over the two wall cells adjacent to the cusp - the 'cusp is the wall maximum' reading; PPM fundamental-only prediction I_1(x_w) / I_0(x_w) < 1 for every x_w
koch_rho.axis_intervals: adjacent axis nulls of the definition-v3 null list (the null list includes nulls outside the straight section inside the search window); when no neighbouring null exists the window edge / grid edge bounds the interval

descriptors_v3.hemp_like_rule: a design is HEMP-like iff it has at least one wall cusp inside the straight dielectric and every such cusp has rho_conservative >= 1.5 (the lower end of the DM9-1 anode cusp value 1.53 in Koch's Table 1, rounded)

ppm_prediction.statement: for an infinite single-harmonic PPM stack of pitch L, wall radius r_w, x_w = pi r_w / L: |B|(r_w, z_c) / b_1 = I_1(x_w); |B|(r_w, z_c) / |B|(r_w, stage centre) = I_1(x_w) / I_0(x_w); review section 2.2
ppm_prediction.i1_threshold: I_1(x*) = 1.5 at x* = 1.937318 (r_w / L = 0.616668), computed by bisection on the power series in descriptors.py; the review quotes r_w / L = 0.62 for 1.5x, 0.96 for 4x and 1.30 for 10.6x (I_1 = 4 at x = 3.0130, r_w / L = 0.9591; I_1 = 10.6 at x = 4.0909, r_w / L = 1.3022)
ppm_prediction.why_i1_not_the_realised_ratio: the realised rho divides by the finite-stack axis peak (end effects raise the interior peak above the fitted b_1 by a few percent) and the L1a field has small end-effect harmonics, so rho / I_1(x_w) was 0.88-0.94 for the four sweep-v2 representatives and P2 in the review's Table D

hypothesis.statement: H1: over every wall cusp of the 128 Sobol designs, rho_conservative tracks the PPM prediction I_1(x_w): the least-squares slope of rho on I_1(x_w) through the origin lies in [0.80, 1.00] and at least 80 % of the cusps have rho_conservative / I_1(x_w) within the agreement band. H2: the I_1 threshold predicts the HEMP-like classification: a design with x_w >= x* = 1.937318 (I_1(x_w) >= 1.5) is HEMP-like and a design with x_w < x* is not, with prediction accuracy >= 0.85 over the Sobol designs that have at least one wall cusp. Both are REPORTED tests, not binding gates; the numbers are what the campaign measures.
hypothesis.expected_direction_if_true: rho rises monotonically with x_w and crosses 1.5 near x_w = 1.94 (r_w / L = 0.62); designs inside the sweep-v2 box (x_w <= 1.55, I_1 <= 1.03) never reach 1.5
hypothesis.what_would_falsify: slope outside [0.80, 1.00], fewer than 80 % of cusps in the band, accuracy below 0.85, or HEMP-like designs appearing inside the sweep-v2 box
hypothesis.statistics: slope through the origin, R^2 against that line, median / min / max of rho / I_1, fraction in band, 2x2 confusion table of predicted (I_1 >= 1.5) vs realised (all cusps rho >= 1.5), prediction accuracy, smallest realised HEMP-like x_w and largest non-HEMP-like x_w, x* implied by the fitted slope (I_1(x) = 1.5 / slope)

descriptors_v3.wall_harmonics: B_r(r_w, z) sampled at 401 points between the first and last stage centre (inside the straight dielectric) and fitted by linear least squares to sin/cos pairs at k = 1, 3, 5 times pi / L with the geometric pitch; reported |b_3 / b_1| and |b_5 / b_1| are wall amplitudes (never axis-fitted harmonics extrapolated to the wall; the review documents a 1.7-2.1x error for that shortcut)
descriptors_v3.separatrix_angle: angle_to_wall_normal_deg of definition v3 at every wall cusp (reported)
descriptors_v3.resolution_sensitivity: rho_conservative is computed on the accepted map and on the 2x refined map; the maximum per-design |rho_acc - rho_ref| / rho_ref is reported (the refinement-stability gate on z_c is binding, this is not)
descriptors_v3.profiles: wall |B|, wall B_r, wall B_z and axis B_z on 241 points of the plot window (channel extended by one pitch, clipped to the grid) are stored per design from the accepted map for the dashboard's cusp maps

sampling.algorithm: scrambled Sobol (Joe-Kuo new-joe-kuo-6.21201 direction numbers, Gray-code generation, Matousek linear-matrix scramble + digital shift with SHA-256-derived bits) in experiments.l1a_geometry_sweep_v3.sampling; the first 128 points (a (t, 7, 11)-net) scaled to the variable box

sweep_v2_box.statement: every sweep-v2 variable interval is contained in the v3 interval, so the sweep-v2 region is a subset of the v3 box; Sobol designs that fall inside the sweep-v2 box are flagged inside_sweep_v2_box and pooled with the 96 held-out sweep-v2 designs as the 'sweep-v2 region'

regime_coverage.hemp_like_predicted_where: x_w >= 1.937318, i.e. r_w >= 0.616668 L; with the box above this is r_w >= 2.10 mm at L = 3.4 mm and r_w >= 4.01 mm at L = 6.5 mm (about 37 % of the box volume in (L, r_w))
regime_coverage.why_not_shorter_pitch: the accepted map has dz = 0.4514 mm; 3.4 mm keeps >= 7.5 axial samples per pitch (the review's fits used 8-14) and the 2x refined map >= 15

sampling.bounds_provenance: the upper bounds of chamber_outer_radius_m (4.2 mm), radial_clearance_m (1.6 mm) and magnet_radial_thickness_m (5.0 mm) and the lower bound of stage_pitch_m (3.4 mm) were fixed after six corner solves on 2026-09-03 (largest magnets with and without exit taper at 3 and 5 stages, shortest pitch at largest and smallest radius) that all passed the six sweep-v2 metric gates with margin (boundary_to_peak_ratio <= 0.0212 vs 0.05, topology_confidence >= 0.868 vs 0.5, manufacturing margins >= 50 um); no rho value was looked at when fixing the bounds

geometry.builder: experiments.l1a_geometry_sweep_v3.designs.build_case: the sweep-v2 derivation rules (stage_count = min(5, 3 + int(selector*3)); pitch moved inward by <= 64 ULPs until the v1.1 pitch identity passes; chamber length = stage_count * pitch; injector 8 % of the chamber; exit taper when exit_length_fraction * chamber >= 0.25 mm with exit radius r_w * (1.15 + 0.35 * descriptor) moved inward by <= 128 ULPs for taper continuity; magnet inner radius = max(r_w, exit radius) + dielectric + clearance; magnet axial thickness = pitch * magnet_axial_fraction; shield +0.75 mm, yoke +1.75 mm outside the magnets; alternating full-strength polarity starting with first_polarity)
geometry.stage_count_mapping: min(5, 3 + int(selector*3)) -> 3, 4, 5 stages with equal probability thirds
geometry.length_binary64_policy: the pitch and the four radial variables (chamber_outer_radius_m, dielectric_thickness_m, radial_clearance_m, magnet_radial_thickness_m) and the requested exit radius are represented by their nearest multiple of 2^-40 m (0.91 pm) before the sweep-v2 rules are applied, so every radial sum and stage-centre product is exact in binary64 and the geometry v1.1 ULP identities hold with zero error; the sweep-v2 inward-ULP walks are kept as verification and return at their first iteration. Reason (found on the raw Sobol sample before the shakedown): 22 of 128 raw value sets violate (r_w + d) - r_w == d within 2 ULP purely by rounding once r_w + d exceeds 2^-8 m, which no exit-radius walk can repair; requested and represented values are both recorded
geometry.polarity: alternating full-strength (every stage the same |ampere-turns|); never the weak even stages of four-cell topology search v2

manufacturability_limits_assumed.magnet_material: cft_revival.magnetics.checked_synthetic_smco_like_magnet: synthetic SmCo-like example, remanence 1.05 T at 293.15 K, recoil mu_r 1.05, intrinsic coercivity 1.6 MA/m; NOT a vendor grade; the L1a source is the two equivalent current sheets (Br / mu0 times the magnet axial thickness) smeared over 0.8 mm, scaled by source_strength_scale in [0.75, 1.3] (harmless for topology and rho, which are scale-invariant)
manufacturability_limits_assumed.pole_pieces: soft-iron-assumed regions (mu_r 4000) fill the inter-magnet gaps in the geometry but are source-free vacuum in the L1a field (linear vacuum, no material response)
manufacturability_limits_assumed.feasibility_by_construction: every variable box corner satisfies the geometry v1.1 manufacturing rules (checked in designs.feasibility_report and recorded per design); no design is rejected or resampled

preview.description: geometry v1.1 thin-volume current-equivalent preview; not material-aware

field.statement: the accepted map is the sweep-v2 domain and resolution solved with cft_revival.fields.solve_problem_cpu (the CPU solver whose parity with the sweep-v2 CUDA solves was recorded at 1e-15); the refined map is the same discrete problem at 2x radial and axial intervals; both use the sweep-v2 solver configuration
field.why_the_sweep_v2_domain: the sweep-v2 QoIs (nearest-node samples on this grid) must be reproducible verbatim for the held-out set and comparable across the v2 region and the new designs; a finer accepted grid would cost 8-10x per design and break the 1 h budget

definition_v3_import.source: experiments.cusp_topology_search_v3_1.topology (characterize_map, compare_resolutions, axis_window, bicubic_field) imported unchanged; protocol.json#definition_v3 of that experiment (result commit cec47f12) is the definition authority and is bound by hash in dependency_source_sha256
definition_v3_import.must_equal_v3_1: experiment.policy_from raises if these parameters differ from the v3.1 protocol

sobol_v3.why: the new space-filling sample of the v3 box; the object of every estimand
sobol_v3.keep_paths: every Sobol design stores its separatrix paths (execution.keep_paths_for_sets) so the dashboard can draw the cusp maps of whichever designs turn out HEMP-like

sweep_v2.why: held-out reproduction: the 96 accepted sweep-v2 designs rebuilt and re-solved through the wall-loss geometry screening's identity-proven pipeline (rebuilt hashes == sealed raw record, QoIs replay within the sweep-v2 tolerances, four stored representatives reproduce node-wise, sealed axis nulls match the v3 nulls); they also give the v2-region overlay of the rho vs x_w scatter

estimands.binding_none: no estimand is a gate; all estimands are reported at whatever value the campaign measures
per_design: wall cusps (z_c, |B|, angle) and cells (v3.1 catalogue entry)
rho_downstream / rho_upstream / rho_conservative / rho_wall per cusp
the sweep-v2 QoIs and the six sweep-v2 metric gates
campaign: fraction of Sobol designs with all interior cusps at rho_conservative >= 1.5 (and among designs with at least one cusp)
rho vs x_w scatter against I_1(x_w): slope, R^2, band fraction, confusion table, accuracy, realised threshold band
the feasible HEMP-like sub-region: ranges of x_w, r_w / L, x_m and the stage / cusp histograms of the HEMP-like designs
count of five-stage designs with exactly four wall cusps that are HEMP-like
count of sweep-v2-region designs (held-out 96 + Sobol designs inside the v2 box) reaching rho >= 1.5 and their maximum rho
wall-cusp count histogram and the fraction with N - 1 cusps for N stages
pooled rho_wall and the number of cusps that are the wall |B| maximum of their neighbourhood
held-out reproduction counts for the sweep-v2 set

binding_integrity.all_declared_designs_resolved: every declared design (128 Sobol + 96 sweep-v2) built / rebuilt, solved on both maps and characterized (no exclusions)
binding_integrity.identity_proven: every design's geometry / source / config / case hashes equal the frozen design authorities; sweep-v2 designs additionally equal the sealed raw record
binding_integrity.sweep_v2_gates_verbatim: every design passes the six sweep-v2 metric gates with their recorded definitions: boundary_to_peak_ratio <= 0.05, relative_residual_l2 <= 1e-10, flux_reconstruction_identity_t_per_m <= 1e-8, source_representation_error <= 0.25, topology_confidence >= 0.5, min(radial, axial manufacturing margin) >= 0; the seventh sweep-v2 gate (cpu_cuda_parity) has no CUDA solve to compare in this CPU-only campaign and is replaced by determinism_replay
binding_integrity.solver_converged_both_maps: the accepted and the refined CPU solves report converged = true
binding_integrity.every_null_converged: definition v3: every axis null in every map converged, X-type, classifications agree
binding_integrity.every_trace_terminates_cleanly: definition v3: every separatrix terminates as wall or domain_z
binding_integrity.every_wall_trace_flux_consistent: definition v3: every wall-reaching trace agrees with the flux root within 5e-5 m
binding_integrity.refinement_stability: catalogue stability: same axis-null count, same wall-reaching count, |dz_k| and |dz_c| <= 0.25 mm between the accepted and the 2x refined map for every design
binding_integrity.held_out_sweep_v2_reproduction: for every sweep-v2 design: rebuilt hashes equal the sealed record, the re-solved QoIs replay within the sweep-v2 scale-aware tolerances, the four stored representatives reproduce node-wise, and the sealed axis nulls inside the v3 window are in bijection with the v3 nulls within 0.25 mm
binding_integrity.determinism_replay: re-solving and re-characterizing the replay designs in the main process reproduces the worker's canonical topology/descriptor payload bytes exactly and the accepted psi grid node-for-node
binding_integrity.hash_bindings: protocol, experiment code, dependency sources, field pipeline sources and sealed-source identities equal the preregistered authorities

shakedown.purpose: Exercise the complete production path (Sobol sampling, v3 builder, sweep-v2 rebuild with identity proof, CPU solves at both resolutions, sweep-v2 QoIs and gates, tracing grids, definition-v3 characterization import, stability, held-out correspondence, Koch rho and PPM descriptors, wall harmonics, profiles, gates, dataset, CSV, v3 catalogue, publication through the shared ExperimentRuntime into a temporary root, validate_bundle) on REAL designs of both sets before the preregistration freeze.
shakedown.design_rule: Sobol: the design with the largest x_w, the design with the smallest x_w, the five-stage design with the largest x_w, one design inside the sweep-v2 box, the first and the last of the sequence (duplicates removed); sweep-v2: 000 (representative with stored map, lowest field energy), 065 (five-stage strongest-centreline representative), 095 (last of the sorted list)
prepare_requires: experiment_code_sha256, dependency_source_sha256 and field_pipeline_source_sha256 equal the current sources

execution.cpu_budget_note: at most 6 of the 24 logical CPUs (a screening campaign uses 12 and the GPU runs PIC); every solve is cft_revival.fields.solve_problem_cpu; wall-clock budget 1 h
execution.parallel_determinism_rule: each design's record is a pure function of (protocol, design identity); workers return canonical payloads with their SHA-256; the main process re-solves and re-characterizes the replay designs and requires byte-identical canonical payloads

per_design: artifacts/designs/<set>/<design_id>.json (identity, solver evidence, sweep QoIs and gates, both characterizations, stability, held-out comparison, descriptors on both maps, profiles; separatrix paths for Sobol designs and sweep-v2 representatives)
artifacts/fields/<set>/<design_id>.json.gz (accepted psi grid as gzip of canonical JSON; payload SHA-256 recorded in the design record)

catalogue.label: SCREENING_L1A_FIELD_SEPARATRIX_CUSP_TOPOLOGY
catalogue.consumer_contract: one entry per design (set_id, design_id, label, geometry, design values, x_w, axis nulls, wall cusps with z_c / |B| / angle, cells with mirror descriptors, per-cusp Koch rho readings, hemp_like_all_cusps, inside_sweep_v2_box, stable flag) so a future wall-loss screening can stratify its launch design by regime (sweep-v2 region vs HEMP-like) and define cells by actual separatrix intersections; consumers must carry the label SCREENING_L1A_FIELD_SEPARATRIX_CUSP_TOPOLOGY and must not read rho or the mirror descriptors as probabilities
catalogue.loader: experiments.l1a_geometry_sweep_v3.catalogue.load_catalogue (validates the v3.1 structure through the imported validator plus the v3 extension against the bundle manifest)

claim_boundary.field_level: L1a linear-vacuum equivalent-current FDM (not P2, not hardware-valid); the declared soft-iron pole pieces and yoke are source-free vacuum in the field
claim_boundary.definition_source: cusp topology search v3.1 (HEMP/DCFT literature definition) for cusps and cells; Koch et al. IEPC-2007-110 for rho
claim_boundary.iron_sensitivity: not tested; the review (section 5.3) finds iron changes the amplitude, not the cusp positions or wall-field shape, at x_w ~ 1, and recommends a material-aware check before any absolute field, mirror ratio or rho-based claim for r_w / L > 0.5

l1b_p2_confirmation.statement: for every design with r_w / L > 0.5 the TWT/PPM review recommends an L1b (cft_revival.material_fields, screening-only) or P2 (adaptive FEM with iron) confirmation of rho before it is used in a design decision; this campaign records the recommendation and runs no material-aware solve
l1b_p2_confirmation.consumer: a future L1b/P2 confirmation campaign on the HEMP-like representatives of the v3 catalogue

usable_as: regime-stratified cell definitions for a future wall-loss screening (labelled)
evidence about the original study's design space (which regime it covered and which it did not)
the design list for an L1b/P2 confirmation of rho in the HEMP-like regime
